in_latin.name: Berkley
in_latin.meaning: Nomen Anglicum de loco Bercleri in Anglia
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Berkley originem habet a loco Bercleri in Anglia, ubi anno 1066 castellum eodem nomine stabat. Nomen de la Bereclièr, quod significat 'de regione musci', est nomen Francogallicum Anglicum quod pertinet ad Guillelmum Pictavensem, filium Guillelmi Pictavensis, qui castellum Bercleri ab Eduardo Rege acceptum habuit. Guillelmus Pictavensis fuit filius Guillelmi Pictavensis, qui erat frater Edwardi Regis. Edwardus Rex erat filius Edwardi Odibarti et Agatha Londiniensis. Edwardus Odibartus erat filius Alexandri Odibarti et Elizabetae Londiniensis. Alexander Odibartus erat filius Edwardi Philargyri et Elizabetae Londiniensis. Edwardus Philargyrus erat filius Edwardi Odibarti et Elizabetae Londiniensis. Edwardus Odibartus erat filius Edwardi de Northampton et Elizabetae Londiniensis. Edwardus de Northampton erat filius Edwardi Odibarti et Elizabetae Londiniensis.

in_english.name: Berkley
in_english.meaning: English name derived from the place name Berkeley in England, meaning 'from the brushwood clearing'
in_english.long_meaning: The name Berkley has its origins in England and is associated with the place name Berkeley, where in 1066 a castle of the same name stood. The name de la Bereclièr, meaning 'from the brushwood clearing', is a French-Anglican name that pertains to William Peverel, son of William Peverel, who received the castle of Berkeley from King Edward. William Peverel was the son of William Peverel, who was the brother of King Edward. King Edward was the son of Edward Odiham and Agatha of London. Edward Odiham was the son of Alexander Odiham and Elizabeth of London. Alexander Odiham was the son of Edward Philargy and Elizabeth of London. Edward Philargy was the son of Edward Odiham and Elizabeth of London. Edward Odiham was the son of Edward of Northampton and Elizabeth of London. Edward of Northampton was the son of Edward Odiham and Elizabeth of London.
